subject: Final-day log cutoff / retro-capture semantics for SOC 2 reporting period
messages:
From: Sam Tanner <sam.tanner@acuityaudit.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jin Park <jin.park@clientcorp.com>
Date: 2025-06-22 08:12:00 -0000
Subject: SOC 2 period: final-day inclusivity and retro log capture

Hi Grace,

Quick question as we finalize our test plan for ClientCorp's SOC 2 Type II: the report period ends on 2025-06-30. Can you confirm whether events with timestamps exactly at 2025-06-30T23:59:59.999Z (UTC) are treated as "in period" for evidence collection?

Also, ClientCorp's environment performs delayed log ingestion for some forwarders (up to 12 hours). Do you have a documented policy or manifest that states whether "late-arriving" logs that are reconciled into the system within X hours are included in the point-in-time evidence for the period-end? If you do include them, can you outline the window and provide the log_manifest for 2025-06-30 (or point us to where we can pull it)?

We attached a brief evidence request list (SOC2_evidence_request_list.pdf) — please let us know what you can provide and whether a signed bridge letter will be required to document any agreed-upon inclusion window.

Thanks,
Sam Tanner
Senior Audit Manager
Acuity Audit LLP

Attachment: SOC2_evidence_request_list.pdf (1 page)
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sam Tanner <sam.tanner@acuityaudit.com>
Cc: Jin Park <jin.park@clientcorp.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2025-06-22 12:37:00 -0000
Subject: Re: SOC 2 period: final-day inclusivity and retro log capture

Hi Sam — thanks for the clear questions. Short answers up front:

- Final-day inclusivity: Yes, for hosted Redwood services we treat timestamps using strict UTC semantics and consider events with timestamps up to and including 2025-06-30T23:59:59.999999Z as in-scope for the period.

- Late-arriving logs: We operate a two-tier approach: immediate event logging (primary) and a bounded reconciliation window for ingestion pipelines (secondary). For the hosted control plane used by ClientCorp, we accept late-arriving log records into the operational index for up to 18 hours after the event timestamp for forensic reconciliation. Records reconciled within that 18-hour window are marked with a reconciliation flag and included in period evidence if they were committed to the primary store before the reconciliation cutoff.

I'm attaching a CSV manifest for 2025-06-30 that lists the high-level log buckets and ingestion policies (log_manifest_20250630.csv). It shows which streams had backfill behavior documented and the reconciliation cutoff timestamps.

That said, for formal SOC 2 test procedures we typically document the reconciliation window in a bridge letter so the auditor has an explicit agreement from the customer on inclusion. If ClientCorp is comfortable with the 18-hour window, we can prepare a bridge_letter_draft.docx for signature. Karthik / Marissa — tagging you to confirm the wording around the reconciliation flag and to confirm whether the 18-hour window applies to Dedicated or Private deployments for ClientCorp's contract.

Regards,
Grace O'Connor
Head of Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
+1 415 555 0123

Attachments: log_manifest_20250630.csv (CSV, 1 file)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>, Sam Tanner <sam.tanner@acuityaudit.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Jin Park <jin.park@clientcorp.com>
Date: 2025-06-23 09:20:00 -0000
Subject: Re: SOC 2 period: final-day inclusivity and retro log capture

Adding a technical note: the 18-hour reconciliation window Grace cited is specific to Redwood's hosted ingestion pipeline where we run a short-lived staging queue before committing events to the immutable ledger. For ClientCorp's Dedicated cluster (which I know they're evaluating), the reconciliation window can be configured by the customer and may be shorter; defaults are 6 hours for Dedicated.

Operationally, reconciled records are stamped with commit_timestamp (the time they are persisted into the immutable store) and with original_event_timestamp. For SOC evidence we provide both timestamps and a reconciliation flag so the auditor can see whether a record was late-arriving and when it was committed.

Marissa — can you confirm we have the bridge letter template that spells out the chosen reconciliation window and the explicit commit_timestamp inclusion rule? If so, please attach the template and propose a short paragraph we can use for ClientCorp's sign-off.

Thanks,
Karthik
VP, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jin Park <jin.park@clientcorp.com>, Sam Tanner <sam.tanner@acuityaudit.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2025-06-25 16:44:00 -0000
Subject: Re: SOC 2 period: final-day inclusivity and retro log capture

Jin / Sam — attached is a short bridge letter draft that states:

"For the reporting period ending 2025-06-30, Redwood Inference agrees that events with original event timestamps on or before 2025-06-30T23:59:59.999999Z UTC and committed to the Redwood immutable store within 18 hours of the event timestamp will be treated as in-scope for period evidence. Reconciled records will include both the original_event_timestamp and commit_timestamp and a reconciliation flag; the commit_timestamp is the authoritative time used for evidence collection."

If ClientCorp wants a shorter window for Dedicated or Private, we can amend the wording; otherwise please sign and return and we'll confirm the manifest entries and provide the signed copy for your SOC 2 binder.

Marissa Cole
Manager, Compliance Programs
Redwood Inference

Attachment: bridge_letter_draft.docx (Word doc, 1 file)
